key_insight: Quantum models can leak hidden behaviors through public interfaces, and quantum neural networks preserve hidden-task information much more strongly than classical networks in the task-channel setting.
engineering_relevance: This raises a supply-chain security risk for quantum ML systems while also suggesting a controllable mechanism for routing hidden information in quantum information workflows.
method: Study two subliminal-learning pathways: an auxiliary channel on random inputs and a restricted task channel with disjoint hidden/public tasks.
Compare classical neural networks and quantum neural networks under the same distillation setup.
Use a geometric view based on teacher drift magnitude and the visible fraction of hidden-task-relevant drift.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports efficient auxiliary-channel subliminal learning for both model types, but strong architecture dependence in the task channel, with QNNs retaining most hidden-task signal while classical networks transmit little.
watch_item: Results are architecture- and interface-dependent, so hidden-information transfer may be highly sensitive to model design and public-task formulation.
